High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard on I.A. No. 32305/2024, which is an application for amendment in the memo of appeal as well as application for suspension of sentence.
For the reasons stated in the application, I.A. No. 32305/2024 is allowed and learned counsel for the appellant is directed to carry out necessary amendment during the course of the day.

Also heard on I.A. No. 13446/2023, which is first application filed under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.
for suspension of custodial sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant- Golu Nut.

Appellant stands convicted vide judgment dated 25/01/2023 passed by Additional Sessions Judge,
Jaysingh Nagar, District Shahdol in S.T. No. 16/2020 for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) and 376(3) of the IPC and under Section 5(j)(ii) and 5(L) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced him to undergo RI for 3 years, 10 years and 20 years and to pay fine amount of Rs.1,000/- for each offence respectively with default stipulation.
The prosecution story found to be proved is that the complainant PW-3 alongwith her five children went to her parents house at Bihar for 2 CRA-7231-2023 attending last rituals of her father.

sentences.text: On 29.09.2018 she alongwith her two sons went to jungle to graze buffaloes.
At that time her three daughters were at home.
When she returned home in the evening, she found that one of her daughters (prosecutrix) was missing.
She asked in the locality for her whereabouts but could not be traced.
Thereafter, it came to knowledge that the prosecutrix has left the home and taken away Rs.20,000/- and silver ornaments.
She apprehended that some unknown person by alluring her took away.

The prosecutrix was recovered at 20/03/2020 from the possession of the appellant at Janakpur and after completion of investigation, PS Sidhi registered a case as mentioned Golu Nut vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59898507/
1 hereinabove.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in the alleged offence.

It is also submitted that the prosecutrix is having love affair with the appellant and she had gone with the appellant on her own volition and she remained with the appellant for considerable time and visited several places, however, at that time she has neither raised any alarm nor tried to escape from the appellant, which clearly indicates that she was the consenting party.

On the basis of X- ray report (Ex. P/15), age of the prosecutrix is determined about 18 to 20 years, therefore, learned trial Court has committed grave error in convicting the appellant for commission of offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC as well as under Section 5(j)(ii) and 5(L) read with section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There are fair chances of success of this appeal and if custodial sentence of the appellant is not suspended, then purpose for filing of this appeal will be frustrated.
This 3 CRA-7231-2023 appeal is of the year 2023 and there is not possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.

Under these circumstances,
learned counsel for the appellants prays for suspension of custodial sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application by contending that there is ample evidence available on record to connect the appellant with the alleged offence,
therefore, no case for suspension of custodial sentence and grant of bail to the appellant is made out.

Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the fact that prosecutrix has remained in the company of appellant for considerable time and at that time neither she has raised any alarm nor tried to escape from the appellant, in the considered opinion of this Court till disposal of this appeal, execution of jail sentence awarded to the appellant under the impugned judgment deserves to be suspended.

Therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, I.A.
No.13446/2023 is allowed.

It is directed appellant be released on bail subject to depositing fine amount (if already not deposited) and upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for securing his presence before the trial Court concerned on 05/02/2025 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard and execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended during pedency of this appeal.
Accordingly, the aforesaid application stands allowed and disposed of.
4 CRA-7231-2023 List this appeal for final hearing in due course.
(SUSHRUT ARVIND DHARMADHIKARI)

(ANURADHA  JUDGE JUD  skt Golu Nut vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59898507/
